approval_source.question_set: Whether the node unit keeps Restart=no (host_files.py:177) after the sentry was not restarted on 2026-11-10 (user, 13 November 2026: 'proceed with your recommendations on the remaining items')

reason: Staging sentry startup failure of 2026-11-10 (BOUNDED_STARTUP_FAILURE, height 173,074); root cause in draft PR #135, fix in PR #136. The supervisor exited at +92 s and systemd did not restart it; the replacement validator then ran without a sentry. With the checkpoint a restart would now pass its startup check. The E04 records of 4 and 5 November (P01_E04_VERIFIER_CLASS, P01_E04_CHECKTX_VERIFIER, P01_E04_CHECKTX_HELPER_FAILURES, P01_E04_NODE_WARNINGS) did not authorize an automatic restart and left the unit at Restart=no; this decision changes that for the sentry and endpoint only.

decisions.question: Validator unit
decisions.selected: Keep Restart=no: a validator starts only by hand, after the signing guard and the sentry hold
decisions.rule: No automatic restart may start a validator.

decisions.question: Sentry and endpoint units
decisions.selected: Restart=on-abnormal, RestartSec=30, StartLimitIntervalSec=600, StartLimitBurst=3, with the unit-failure alert unchanged: the sentry and endpoint restart after a crash by signal (an OOM kill, a segfault, a kill); every classified failure stays down for its runbook
decisions.rule: A start that fails three times in 10 minutes stays down and pages; the restart never wipes or repairs state. Changing host_files.py so the sentry and endpoint units render the restart settings above, and the validator unit keeps Restart=no; it reaches the hosts with the next sealed bundle. systemd counts every start against the limit, so a deliberate start (an operator's, the staging agent's start command, a drill's) runs systemctl reset-failed first: the limit bounds only the unit's own restarts on failure, and the monitor's restart-loop alert still counts every start. The supervisor exits 1 for every failure class (the class is in its report, not its exit status), so systemd cannot tell an upgrade halt or an integrity failure from any other exit; Restart=on-abnormal restarts only crashes by signal. The CI upgrade drill (run 43544759514) showed Restart=on-failure restarting an old release at its upgrade halt until the start limit refused the new release's start.

does_not_authorize: installing the changed unit on a host outside a sealed bundle and its approved install
